title: Holistic Capacity Briefing Slate — Dedicated GPU Pool Controls
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Create a compact, operational-first UI 'briefing slate' for Dedicated GPU capacity that surfaces a single-screen snapshot and quick-controls for: pool health (per-card and aggregate), autoscaling policy presets, burst capacity toggles, and a cost delta preview. The slate is intended for platform engineers and SREs who need to triage capacity issues rapidly and make short-cycle policy changes without leaving the console. Key goals: immediate signal clarity, safe defaults for runtime changes, lightweight rollback paths, and clear unit-cost implications for any action.
comments: 2026-02-12: Initial whiteboard sketches created — focused on a top-line 'capacity fingerprint' and a set of 3 micro-controls for autoscale/burst/cost-preview. Saved sketches to Drive (see links).

2026-02-18: PM sync with Priya Kapoor — agreed to include 'cost delta preview' in the brief to reduce accidental cost spikes. PM asked for rollout gating for canary traffic. Action: define rollout control affordance.

2026-02-27: Feasibility call with Eng (Ethan Morales) — kernel-level changes not required for UI toggles; need API endpoints for safe rollback and audit events (ENG-2854). Eng requested designs for edge cases where autoscale fails to provision.

2026-03-05: Design critique — UX team recommended stronger visual separation between health signals (thermal/latency/errors) and policy settings. Also flagged potential accessibility contrast issues on the delta chip. Assigned accessibility pass.
2026-03-08: Prototype update pushed to Figma — added inline confirmations for burst toggles and a cost impact micrograph. Shared with stakeholders for comment.
2026-03-10: Security review note from Security (Marta Alvarez) — audit logs + KMS metadata required on any policy change for Private deployments; added to acceptance criteria and ENG tasks.
2026-03-11: PM review — approved high-level flow, requested additional microcopy for 'safety window' and 'expected latency impact'.
2026-03-12: Submitted final slate for Engineering review and created GitHub PR for console component skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rconsole/pull/8892
decisions: Use a single-line 'capacity fingerprint' header summarizing Load (P99 token latency), Utilization (%), and Health (error rate) with color-coded states.
Autoscale controls will be provided as three presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with an 'Advanced' modal for full policy editing to reduce accidental misconfiguration.
Burst capacity will be a time-limited toggle (0-60 minutes) with an immediate cost-delta preview and required two-step confirmation when estimated cost > $50/hour.
All changes to autoscale/burst must emit audit events compatible with Private/KMS logging requirements (per Security input).
Accessibility pass completed: contrast ratios, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader labels included in the prototype.

Create the Advanced Policy modal spec and microcopy (owner: Aisha Rao) — due 2026-03-16.
Implement unit-cost calculation service hookup for cost-delta preview (owner: ENG-2999).

acceptance_criteria: Single-screen slate renders with capacity fingerprint and policy controls at small/medium widths.
Autoscale presets apply via API and changes appear in audit logs with KMS metadata for Private tenants.
Burst toggle shows accurate cost-delta preview within 5% of backend calc for sample workloads.
Two-step confirmation appears for high-cost actions and can be bypassed by users with 'ops-admin' role.
Console unit tests and basic e2e tests for the brief and Advanced Policy modal are merged (PR linked).
